response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL GROUP BY production_type_code), base AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS baseline FROM t), kept AS (SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price, base.baseline FROM t CROSS JOIN base WHERE base.baseline IS NOT NULL AND t.avg_price > base.baseline), km AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS kept_mean FROM kept), fin AS (SELECT k.avg_price, k.baseline, km.kept_mean FROM kept k CROSS JOIN km WHERE k.avg_price > km.kept_mean) SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS avg_type_average_price, AVG(avg_price - baseline) AS avg_above_baseline, AVG(avg_price - kept_mean) AS avg_above_kept_mean FROM fin

assumptions.assumption: Types whose products all have NULL unit_price have no average and are excluded from the baseline and from every later step.
If the baseline does not exist or no types remain after filtering, the query still returns one row, with NULL values.
